title: Guide - Calming an Anxious Heart - Breathe and be still

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Calming an Anxious Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Breathe and Be Still. <short pause> If your heart is racing, or your body feels ready to run, you are in the right place. <short pause> We'll slow down a little at a time.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Start with what is solid. <short pause> Press your feet softly into the floor, or your hands into whatever is beneath them. <short pause> Feel it push back. <short pause> It is holding. <short pause> Press once more... <short pause> and let go.

An anxious body is trying to protect you. <short pause> It quickens the breath and tightens the muscles, as if there were something to fight, or somewhere to flee. <short pause> You don't need to be angry with it. <short pause> You can thank it for trying... <short pause> and show it that this moment can be slower.

God's people once stood in a place with nowhere to run. <short pause> The sea was in front of them, and an army was coming up behind. <short pause> They were very afraid. <short pause> And Moses said to them, in Exodus, chapter fourteen, verse fourteen...
The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Hold your peace. <short pause> They still had a sea to walk through, and soon they would take the next step. <short pause> But the saving did not depend on their strength. <short pause> Before they moved at all, God had already taken their side.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let's give those words to your breath. <short pause> We won't take big breaths, only soft ones, with a longer breath out. <short pause> If that ever feels uncomfortable, breathe as you normally do, and simply listen. <short pause> There is no wrong way to rest here.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Breathe in softly... <short pause> the Lord will fight for me. <short pause> And breathe out slowly... <short pause> I can hold my peace. <short pause> Again, breathe in... <short pause> the Lord will fight for me. <short pause> And out, all the way... <short pause> I can hold my peace.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Keep the breath easy, and let the words grow shorter. <short pause> Breathe in... <short pause> He fights. <short pause> Breathe out... <short pause> I am still. <short pause> Breathe in... <short pause> He fights. <short pause> Breathe out, long and slow... <short pause> I am still.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Now, as you keep breathing, let one part of you stand down. <short pause> Your eyebrows, which have been on watch. <short pause> Your tongue, resting in your mouth. <short pause> The muscles of your stomach. <short pause> The space between your shoulders. <short pause> They don't all have to soften. <short pause> One is a beginning.

You may still feel some of the fear. <short pause> That doesn't mean this isn't working, and it doesn't mean your faith is small. <short pause> The people by the sea were trembling when those words were spoken to them. <short pause> God did not wait for them to feel brave before He helped them.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Take one more breath with the whole verse. <short pause> The Lord shall fight for you... <short pause> and ye shall hold your peace. <short pause> For this minute, there is no argument you have to win... <short pause> and no future you have to defend.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, my defender, <short pause> my body is tired of bracing. <short pause> Stand where I have been standing guard. <short pause> Slow what is racing in me. <short pause> When it is time to take a step, show me the step. <short pause> Until then, teach me to be still beside You. <short pause> Amen.

You can take this with you into the next hard moment, in a hallway, in the car, or in a waiting room. <short pause> Feet on the ground. <short pause> A long breath out. <short pause> And three quiet words... <short pause> hold your peace. <short pause> Go gently.
